report:
## Conclusion

The claim that eating dark chocolate lowers stroke risk is **plausible and supported by observational evidence, but not proven causally**.

**Observational data:** Multiple prospective cohort studies consistently link higher chocolate consumption (especially dark/flavonoid-rich chocolate) with reduced stroke risk. A meta-analysis of five cohort studies (4,260 stroke cases) found roughly a 19% lower risk of stroke in the highest vs. lowest chocolate consumption groups, with no significant difference by stroke subtype (https://www.neurology.org/doi/10.1212/WNL.0b013e31826aacfa; https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0021915017300941). A broader meta-analysis of coronary heart disease, stroke, and diabetes similarly found inverse associations, though benefits plateaued around 3–6 servings/week (https://www.mdpi.com/2072-6643/18/4/636).

**Mechanistic plausibility:** Cocoa flavanols may lower blood pressure, reduce inflammation, improve endothelial function, and inhibit platelet aggregation—all mechanisms relevant to stroke prevention (https://www.rupahealth.com/post/dark-chocolate-and-cardiovascular-diseases-insights-from-a-mendelian-randomization-study).

**Causal evidence is weaker:** A 2023 Mendelian randomization study using genetic variants associated with dark chocolate intake did not find strong causal evidence linking genetically predicted dark chocolate consumption to reduced cardiovascular disease risk overall, suggesting confounding (e.g., healthier lifestyles among chocolate consumers) may explain some cohort findings (https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10781976/).

**Bottom line:** Moderate dark chocolate intake is associated with lower stroke risk in observational studies, and biological mechanisms support plausibility, but genetic/causal studies raise doubt about a direct causal effect. Chocolate should not be viewed as a proven stroke-prevention strategy—rather as one dietary factor among many, and excess consumption (due to sugar/fat content) could offset any benefit.
